correctness.rationale: Rectangular-closure criterion follows from monotone grade dominance, and a constructed polygonal path realizes every closed-prefix order. Antichain closure is interval hull, yielding the 2^(n-1) count. Distinct homology degrees in an explicit wedge of simplicial spheres force distinct positive-degree combinatorial barcode orders. Affine arrival times are max(i,z-wi); their pair-order walls are z=j+wi for i<j. Standard line arrangement bound is 1+M+choose(M,2), M=choose(n,2). Exact inequalities rule out a six-point monotone order from all positive-slope affine lines. CHECK.py exact finite experiments independently agree but do not substitute for the proofs.

value.rationale: Conjecture 7.1 of the 2026 primary motivates counting directed-path barcode classes. The present natural one-critical family quantifies a sharp invariant loss when only affine lines are sampled: exponentially many positive-degree combinatorial barcode types versus at most quartically many line orders, with an elementary first failure at six points. It makes the qualitative limitation measurable for arbitrary n and isolates the strict-event scope; no broad k-critical theorem is asserted.
